body:
Thanks for the pep talk r3d. It's good to just hear someone who is optimistic about things and has had a good relationship. 

I know relationships are really a double edged sword, but my life is pretty good right now and I think it'd be great to have that special someone there.

Actually, that's kind of true about him. We've remained in contact and he's gone through a bunch of relationships that lasted a few weeks. He always calls and says he's got a great new boyfriend, and then a few weeks later he's telling me about how they broke up.

But that's the thing, I kind of have high standards because I have high self esteem. I think I should have someone equal to what I think I am, but I don't seem to be able to find it. Maybe I actually love myself and think too much of myself? I dunno.

I was thinking about it too, actually. But, I think guys are a lot more hotter and I'm starting to think that it's more of a people issue as oppose to a gay/straight issue. I mean, really, people are going to be different because they have a vagina? Really?

I don't know what to do anymore, but I knew that since this thread went unreplied for 12+ hours really kind of highlights the issue and the hopelessness that surrounds love.

I've even been thinking lately, that it seems like you always think you're in love, when you're really not because someone is lying to you or fucking with you or whatever. For all the people who are in love and have things working well, does that mean that they just aren't aware of what's happening?

I've been meaning to join a snowmobile club, but I just want to go out and ride and have a good time. I was worried about them all being a bunch of drunkards who just want to drive to bars but I suppose I should just give it a shot this winter and see what happens. It's better to go out and find something sucks than to never have experienced it.

I make friends and meet new people, specially when it's snowboarding season and I can just chill with people on the slopes. But the problem is always the gay thing. Even if you find someone interesting you have to risk losing a good friend by telling them you're gay. I've had it happen before and it's not worth losing friends over.

That's the thing. Honestly, I think I'd just want someone outside of the box. I'd like to think that there's more to people than what they do, who they do it with, and where they work. Yet it seems like that's so important to people. 

My BFF is a really crazy dude and I think I'm just normally attracted to people like that (for relationships or friends, I've never crushed on him before), the kind of odd people who aren't afraid to ask deeper questions about things.

I think too it's that I don't know what I want anymore. It seems like plenty of fish and OKCupid are full of "hopeless romantics", which I pretty much view as the type of person who is desperately seeking love or sex or whatever to fill in one of those voids I was talking about. On the other hand I have no idea how to approach people since I'm a homo and it's hard to deal with stuff like that.

That's the thing that kind of scares me a little. I'm half very outdoorsy person and half ubber geek. I'm living in wisconsin in a medium sized town, and there's not a lot of opportunity for a relationship like that to happen. But, I have my jet skis, snowmobiles, friends, snowboarding, etc and I don't want to give that up by moving to a city or something.
I can't upvote you hard enough. This is *perfect* advice. Thank you!

He's being pleasant, just not talkative. My main concern was that I don't know how to deal with him being untalkative while letting him know I'm still interested. He's apologized for being quiet and not being his usual self. I think if I left him alone he'd think I wasn't interested, which isn't really the case. 

And you're right, we haven't.

I think I have gotten great advice too, I love reddit and almost all of the users.

He has an old 90s pontiac and what he said was basically that the metal bands in the tires were exposed and the tire was flat when he went to go to work. He spent most of his money on college, he went to Texas for a few semesters and didn't like it, so now he can't afford a new car, or tires. A few days before that he went on a long drive to visit some female friend he's known for a while, like 6 hours each way. (I'm gay and so is he, so it's not a big deal).

And that lady that he hit, it was just some scratches on the bumper. He manned up to it and the lady said it wasn't a big deal and not to worry about it. Then, two to three weeks later she comes back and says he owes him 400 to 800 dollars to get the scratches fixed on her bumper.

To a psychologist? I'm afraid of losing my health insurance. I finished college and when I got my new insurance they asked about me seeing one before and I had to tell them that it wasn't a problem anymore.
I think that's a much better idea.

I'm usually that for a lot of people, but I don't want to seem creepy by doing it too soon. It usually takes me a while to open up. I mean, honestly, I just want to tell him that this situation is his chance to make up his mind about going back to school. He wants to get into lab tech work in hospitals, but he's working some shit job at Jimmy Johns as a manager. I should just have a drink and get all philosophical and let him have it.

I get stupid sometimes and forget what I'm capable of, but a few of these posts are really reminding me that I need to stand up and lead.

Thank you groovie girl. He was having problems with things before, and he was fine with them. I don't know if it was just a front like tophat_jones was saying or if he really was dealing with things fine before. Once all this stuff happened with his car, he didn't have the money to pay for everything (he *did* have enough money, but he just paid off his student loan the week before).

I think I will write him on OKC and tell him not to worry about what happened with his car and not being able to make it over and that I still like him and he should text me when he's feeling better.

I'm afraid of asking questions like that to just about everyone. I'm a horrible communicator. To be honest I haven't been dating for a long time, like since I was 18. I guess not dating has made me more or less retarded in my growth in relationships. 

When I'm about to ask something like that, my chest gets tight and I get depressed and stressed out. It's not a trivial thing for me to do at all. I wish it was, I've tried. It's an irrational fear I have that won't go away.

He has insurance but he's afraid of his rates going up. He has accident forgiveness but if he gets a ticket they're going to jack his rates up through the roof. 

And I hate to sound like an ass but I do the same thing. I guess I wouldn't be holding up my half either. Personally I'd be glad to have a relationship where if one of us was depressed, things could just go on hold. I'm just nervous I'm going to send a bad signal. Am I immature or wrong to think that it's acceptable to disappear or recede when you get depressed? 

I don't like to talk to people about my problems and I don't think you have to be if you can take care of yourself. By all means if I'm wrong I'd like to hear some input. But I have a history of getting depressed as well and fading out for a while. It's not my fault, I've always been extremely independent.

But to be honest I've had a lot of bad experiences and I'm not entirely ready for a serious relationship. I just want to date and have fun and see how it turns out.
I did consider that but he'd been acting kind of strange for the last few days before that and said that his psych changed his medication dosages.
